RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.label: two suitors, one heart
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.description: Two colonists court the same person, and one of them asks the lord to settle it.
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.caseText:
{PETITIONER_labelShort} and {OTHER_labelShort} both court {LOVER}, and {LOVER} has not chosen, which is {LOVER}'s right and everyone else's problem. The two of them circle each other at meals, and the colony is waiting to find out where it ends.
{PETITIONER_labelShort} asks the seat to end it first.
How does the lord rule?

li.label: Order {OTHER_labelShort} to give up the suit
li.pastLabel: ordered to give up the suit

li.label: Let them settle it before the court, hand to hand
li.pastLabel: the suit settled hand to hand

li.label: Order them both to leave {LOVER} be
li.pastLabel: both ordered to give up the suit

li.label: Move on to the next case

RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.label: a wrong brought by the one who did it
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.description: A colonist who wronged another comes to court himself, asking the lord to broker the pardon he cannot get alone.
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.caseText:
Every other matter in this hall is brought by the one who was wronged. {PETITIONER_labelShort} brings this one, and {PETITIONER_labelShort} is the one who did it.
{OTHER_labelShort} has not forgiven, and will not, and {PETITIONER_labelShort} has run out of ways to ask. So the wrongdoer stands before the court and asks for a price. Any price. Something that can be paid.
How does the lord rule?

li.label: Set the price: the lash, and the debt dies with it
li.pastLabel: the debt paid under the lash

li.label: Rule that the grudge is deserved
Move on to the next case

RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.label: a debt of gratitude
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.description: A colonist asks that the one who saved their life be honoured for it out loud.
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.caseText:
{PETITIONER_labelShort} is alive because {OTHER_labelShort} went and got {PETITIONER_objective}, and nobody has said anything about it since. {OTHER_labelShort} never asked for anything, which is exactly why {PETITIONER_labelShort} is asking for {OTHER_objective}.
Nobody in this hall is in the wrong. The court hears so little of that, it may take a moment to adjust.
How does the lord rule?

li.label: Honour {OTHER_labelShort} before the court
li.pastLabel: the rescuer honoured before the court

li.label: Rule that saving a life is no more than duty
Move on to the next case

RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.label: an exile at the gate
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.description: A colonist this court banished has come back alone, asking for pardon instead of arriving with a raid.
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.arrivalText:
{PETITIONER_labelShort} is at the gate. This court banished {PETITIONER_objective}, and the sensible thing was to never come back, and here {PETITIONER_pronoun} is anyway, alone and unarmed, asking to be heard.
{PETITIONER_pronoun} will wait {DAYS} days for an audience. What happens if the answer is no, or if no answer comes, is anyone's guess.
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.caseText:
{PETITIONER_labelShort} stands where the banished do not stand twice. The road has taken what it takes, and what is left of {PETITIONER_objective} is asking to come home.
The court that sent {PETITIONER_objective} away is the only one that can unsay it. That is why {PETITIONER_pronoun} is here, and why everyone is watching the seat.
How does the lord rule?

li.label: Pardon {PETITIONER_labelShort}, and let the past lie
Leave the gate shut and say nothing
